catalog_quote: [Bruhn 2014 §III.2.1.1] A syllable minimally consists of an obligatory vowel produced with a particular tone: σ = (C1) (G) V (C2) T ... [§III.2.1.5 Tones] Lotha has a register tone system with three levels (Low, Mid, and High), all of which are manifested on both verbal and nominal roots. It is my impression that minimal pairs/triplets distinguished only by tonal contrasts are rarer in Lotha than in Chungli. ... Still, segmental homophones may be found in Lotha, such as those in the following tables: /o‑kʰuʔ/ L.L ‘trap (n.)’, /o‑kʰuʔ/ L.M ‘wound, fresh injury; scar’, /o‑kʰuʔ/ L.H ‘lung’ ... /ji-aʔ/ H.M ‘come here!’, /ji-aʔ/ L.M ‘go away!’ ... As in Mongsen, the underlying Lotha TBU is the syllable. ... While the resultant vowel may be phonetically long in order to accommodate its tone contour, vowel length is not a contrastive feature in the phonology of Lotha. Word-final open syllables…

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: every sentence of the deciding Bruhn 2014 quotation is verbatim in the text we hold at the stated pages (p.151 syllable canon; pp.157-158 Tones, Tables 122-123), and the Witter 1888 cross-check quote is verbatim in the held archive.org djvu text. (2) Deciding source: a 2014 Berkeley dissertation whose Lotha phonology is the author's own fieldwork -- primary, modern, competent; it states tone is obligatory on every syllable (sigma =..T), three register levels, syllable = TBU, and says nothing about word stress in Lotha. (3) Better/newer sources: Glottolog 5.3 adds Ngullie 2022, a NEHU PhD reference grammar; downloaded its phonology chapter from Shodhganga and read 3.2 (pp.72-90): three register tones H/M/L plus two morphologically derived contours, tone 'determines the semantics of a particular word in each and every utterance', same come/go tonal minimal pair that Witter 188

sources.citation: Ngullie, Yantsubeni. 2022. A descriptive grammar of Lotha. PhD thesis, Department of Linguistics, North-Eastern Hill University, Shillong (supervisor B. Khyriem). hdl:10603/526124 (Shodhganga).
sources.quote: p.73: 'In suprasegmental phonology the feature of tone plays a significant role in the sound system of Lotha. Tone determines the semantics of a particular word in each and every utterance... Lotha has five level tones; thee-way contrast register tones high, mid and low and two contour tones high-rising and low-falling. Contour tone in Lotha is grammatically triggered tone which appears on verbs particularly on the singular marker -a...' p.74 minimal set [jì-a᷆] 'go away' LF vs [jí-a᷄] 'come' HR (= Bruhn Table 123 / Witter's come/go 'stress' pair). p.85: 'Most of the polysyllabic words in Loth
sources.locator: Ch.3 'Phonology of Lotha', 3.2 Suprasegmental phonology pp.72-90: 3.2.1 Tone pp.73-81, 3.2.2 Syllable structure pp.82-90
